chapter_title: 【This Question is So Hard, I Can't Do It】

segments.title: 【This Question is So Hard, I Can't Do It】
segments.content:
Have you ever had this kind of nightmare?

Dreaming you're in an exam room, and you don't know a single answer.

Chen Guiliang was living a real-life version.

After being startled awake, he actually found himself in an exam room!

Did I wake up too fast?

Chen Guiliang looked down at the test paper, carefully examining the information inside the sealed area. At the top of the paper, a line of small text read:

"Longdu City General High School 2003-2004 Academic Year (First Semester) Grade 12 Midterm Exam - Mathematics (Liberal Arts) Paper."

The first semester midterm exam of senior year?

Phew!

Thank goodness, thank goodness, it's not the Gaokao. (Chinese national college entrance examination)

Chen Guiliang instantly felt much more relaxed.

There's a big difference between being dragged straight to the execution ground and getting a suspended sentence.

On the top left and right corners of the desk were an answer sheet and a pencil case, respectively.

Next to the pencil case was a sharpened 2B pencil. A plastic ruler was placed there to keep the pencil from rolling around on the desk.

Chen Guiliang was still holding a gel pen in his hand.

The scene was too real; it couldn't be a dream.

Chen Guiliang glanced at the test paper. He had already finished the multiple-choice section but hadn't started on the fill-in-the-blanks.

As his gaze fell upon the first fill-in-the-blank question, Chen Guiliang's forehead began to bead with sweat. I don't know how to solve this!

"Let P be a moving point on the circle x²+y²=1. The minimum distance from point P to the line 3x-4y-10=0 is ____"

Circle (x-0)²+(y-0)²=1²

So the center of the circle is (0,0), radius r=1

The distance from the center to the line is d= |3×0-4×0-10| /√[3²+(-4)²]= 

Since d > r, the line is outside the circle. The minimum distance from P to the line is d-r = 1

Back then, he definitely would have known how to solve it; after all, he got into a first-tier university.

But 22 years had passed, and he had long since returned his math knowledge to his PE teacher.

Chen Guiliang picked up the plastic ruler and, using it as a guide, drew a Cartesian coordinate system on his scratch paper.

Then he racked his brain for a long time, completely unsure of what to do next.

His knowledge of the Cartesian plane was a total blank. The only two phrases he could remember were: "odd changes, even stays the same; for the sign, look at the quadrant."

What tf quadrant am I supposed to be looking at!

He continued to read through the next few questions.

As expected, he didn't understand a single one.

A gentle autumn breeze, carrying a hint of chill, blew in through the doors and windows, yet Chen Guiliang felt his whole body heat up.

From anxiety.

He hadn't felt this anxious in many years.

Sigh.

Forget it, I don't give a damn.

This reincarnation scenario is too damn awkward.

Chen Guiliang looked towards the proctor on the platform, a short, stout, middle-aged man. He recognized him at a glance as his high school politics teacher, but... what was his name again?

It seemed his surname was Gao.

This Teacher Gao was crossing his legs, leisurely smoking a cigarette and looking at his phone. The few students near the platform covered their noses with their left hands to block the secondhand smoke, while their right hands were busy writing and solving problems.

I remember now, this guy's name is Gao Zhan.

His wife, Liu Shuying, was Chen Guiliang's English teacher and homeroom teacher.

Gao Zhan put down his Nokia brick phone and quickly noticed Chen Guiliang looking around. He threw his cigarette butt on the floor, stamped it out, and rapped on the desk as a reminder, "Focus on your test, don't look at other people's papers!"

Chen Guiliang lowered his head, put down his pen, and rubbed his face with both hands.

What should I do?

Turn in a blank paper?

It seemed... that was an option.

It was just a midterm, not the damn Gaokao.

With this nothing-to-lose attitude, Chen Guiliang suddenly felt a sense of relief wash over him, and the anxiety of not knowing the answers vanished.

He even had the leisure to study the desk.

On the desk surface, next to the pencil case, someone had drawn a heart pierced by an arrow. Below the heart was the message "love Weiwei." Someone else had written the word "moron" with an arrow pointing to the previous message.

At the very top of the desk was a four-character doggerel verse: Body in the exam room, mind at the internet cafe. Can't solve a single problem, to hell with it all.

The more Chen Guiliang looked, the more interesting he found it, as if he had truly returned to his school days.

He raised his head and brazenly observed the other students, trying to retrieve more memories of his youth from their familiar yet strange faces.

The student to his left, he didn't know at all.

The student to his right was named Gong, seemed to be the class president of the class next door.

The female student diagonally in front of him was named Wu Meng. She had been a dark horse in the Gaokao, becoming the city's top liberal arts scholar. Later, she seemed to have immigrated to Singapore.

"Chen Guiliang!"

Gao Zhan suddenly bellowed, "If you don't want to take the exam, then turn in your paper! What are you doing looking all over the place?"

"Oh."

Chen Guiliang quickly filled in the answers to the multiple-choice questions on the answer sheet, put his pen and ruler back in the pencil case, and stood up.

This action instantly drew the attention of all the students.

It had only been a little over twenty minutes since the exam started. There was no way he could have finished the questions. Chen Guiliang must be messing around.

"Bring your paper over here," Gao Zhan called out.

Chen Guiliang picked up his test paper and answer sheet, walked over, and placed them neatly on the platform desk.

Gao Zhan glanced at the paper. "Why didn't you do the rest of the questions?"

"I have a headache, I'm sick," Chen Guiliang lied glibly.

Gao Zhan didn't believe such nonsense for a second. He frowned and said, "Take it back and finish the test."

In a situation like this, a normal conversation was impossible.

Even the most tactful person couldn't explain reincarnation, much less complete the test paper.

Math was math. If you didn't know it, you just didn't know it.

Chen Guiliang abruptly bent over, clutching his stomach, his expression pained. "Ouch, my stomach hurts, I need to go to the hospital!"

As he spoke, he bolted for the door.

Before Gao Zhan could even react, Chen Guiliang had vanished through the doorway.

After a moment of stunned silence, Gao Zhan muttered angrily to himself, "He's getting more and more out of line!"

This student, Chen Guiliang, was the biggest headache for him and his wife.

He had a whole pile of disciplinary actions against him and was currently on "probationary school attendance"!

But to say Chen Guiliang was a lost cause wasn't entirely fair; his academic performance was actually decent. He could easily make it into a second-tier university, and with a bit of effort, even a first-tier one.

Out of the classroom and standing in the hallway, Chen Guiliang felt increasingly lost.

If this was a dream, it wouldn't be this real.

It seemed he had... truly returned to 2003.

SARS and all that didn't have much of an impact on this small city, only causing the school to cancel military training for new students.

In a daze, Chen Guiliang went downstairs and arrived at the campus plaza.

The sculpture in the center of the plaza, as well as the nearby library building, had been built just last year at great expense for the school's centennial celebration.

Chen Guiliang felt his pockets.

Inside were a key, a student ID card, a library card, and 13 yuan and 60 cents.

After wandering around the plaza for a bit, Chen Guiliang had no idea where to go.

Out of sheer boredom, he headed toward the library building a few dozen meters away.

Just inside the first-floor lobby, he saw a row of glass display cases exhibiting the works of distinguished alumni through the ages.

Two books were set apart, displayed as the school's showpieces: one was called *Thick Black Theory*, the other *City of Fantasy*.

That these two authors could be brought together, and even placed side by side, was a kind of black humor.

He walked around the display cases and went to the book lending room, only to find the door locked tight.

Chen Guiliang quietly left the library building and strolled toward the boys' dormitory.

It was an old, dormitory-style building, said to have been built in the 70s. Fortunately, it was surrounded by camphor trees, which not only kept it cool in the summer but also free from the nuisance of mosquito bites.

Chen Guiliang had forgotten his dorm number, but walking into the hallway awakened his memory, and he headed straight for his room, 302.

He took out his key, opened the brass lock, and pushed the door open.

An affecting scent, a mixture of smelly feet, sweat, and mustiness, rushed to greet him.

Four bunk beds.

The bed frames were all made of iron, painted green. The green paint had turned a dark, murky green, and in many places, the paint had peeled off, revealing the rusted iron pipes underneath.

On the lower bunk of the bed by the door, a wooden guitar rested on the pillow.

On the desk by the window, there was a copy of *The Legend of a Small Soldier*.

Next to *The Legend of a Small Soldier* was a plastic-framed glass mirror. The back of the mirror was lined with paper featuring *Meteor Garden*.

Chen Guiliang casually picked up the mirror.

Looking at himself, words failed him.

His appearance in high school was, how to put it... somewhat shabby.

Due to long-term malnutrition, he was as thin as a bamboo stick, with hollow cheeks that were quite unsightly. At a height of 1.8 meters, he only weighed 112 jin.

Fortunately, his features were regular, with the foundation of a handsome guy.

He could bounce back by eating more meat. In two or three months, he'd be a handsome fellow again!

But he didn't have the money to eat meat every meal.

His monthly living allowance was 150 yuan.

Calculated at 1 yuan for breakfast, 1.5 yuan for lunch, and 1.5 yuan for dinner, his daily food cost was 4 yuan. A month's worth of meals cost 120 yuan.

But Chen Guiliang also had to save money to buy books and magazines, as well as daily necessities like toothpaste and soap, and essentials like clothes and shoes. He went home at least once a month, and the round-trip bus fare was 8 yuan.

All these daily expenses were covered by his living allowance; his parents wouldn't send any extra money.

Therefore, Chen Guiliang often skipped breakfast, and for lunch and dinner, he would mostly buy the 1-yuan meal (which was all vegetables).

When he was most strapped for cash, he would buy instant noodles by the case.

Those expired instant noodles, if bought in bulk, cost only 30 cents a pack. Once, after eating them for a month straight, the mere smell of instant noodles made Chen Guiliang want to puke!

"I must have been reborn, right?"

"The first order of business after being reborn in high school is to solve the problem of eating meat."

"But where will the money come from?"

Chen Guiliang's gaze fell upon his own bunk.

Against the wall by his bed were neat stacks of books and magazines.

Chen Guiliang took off his shoes, climbed up, and casually pulled out a magazine.

Yilin.

He pulled out another magazine.

The Reader (DuZhe).

He then tipped over a stack of books, and from the spines, he could see the titles: *Big Breasts and Wide Hips*, *Hometown and Alien Land*, *The Ugly Chinaman*, *A Bitter Journey Through Culture*, *Chronicle of Wuni Lake*...

My god, the smell of these is a bit much!

What the hell was I reading when I was young?

For these books, I actually saved money from my meals, tightening my belt and going hungry to buy them.

Chen Guiliang gathered all the magazines, then picked out the works of the aforementioned luminaries.

After a moment's thought, novels like *To Live* and *White Deer Plain* didn't seem necessary to keep either.

From several stacks of books and magazines, Chen Guiliang only kept Haizi's poems, a classical Chinese dictionary, *Guwen Guanzhi*, *General Introduction to the I Ching*, *The Plum in the Golden Vase*, *Critique of Pure Reason*, *Being and Nothingness*, and so on.

Only one of them is useful; the others are just for show, huh? The rest, he planned to sell them all!

Sell them for money to buy meat.

To nourish his weak and skinny little body.

Chen Guiliang tore a few pages from a workbook and used his roommate's calligraphy brush to write: "Old magazines, 20 cents each, 3 for 50 cents, 8 for 1 yuan."

Then he wrote: "Classic and contemporary masterpieces, Chinese and foreign, 3 to 5 yuan each."

He blew on the ink to dry it, then bent down to look under the bed.

Soon, he found a battered old suitcase under the bed.

He didn't know whose it was, but he temporarily commandeered it, filled it with the books and magazines, and dragged it away.

Sell this stuff, and live a different life this time around
